root_idea.summary: The root centers on removing, shaving, or abrading something from the surface of another thing.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends to paring and smoothing by people or wind, to abrasive tools and materials, and in the traditional explanation of سَفِينَةٌ to a craft that skims or pares the surface of water.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole QAC group is a Quran-attested noun with the standard citation form سَفِينَة.

senses.usage_conditions: In the supplied Quranic occurrences, the noun denotes a watercraft.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pare, strip, scrape, abrade, or smooth away a superficial covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of wind removing or pulverizing dust from the earth’s surface; the usage may be intensive or involve several objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The paring, scraping, or shaving of a thing’s exterior.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal expression for removing or cutting away a surface.
Used in the construction describing a ship or boat that catches on the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An adz, axe, or other implement used to hew, pare, shape, or smooth a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The implement may be a carpenter’s adz, a tool for paring palm trunks, or a stone or iron instrument used for shaping and smoothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rough skin used as an abrasive or smoothing material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is described especially as being used on sword hilts or to smooth arrows; the reported material includes rough animal or fish skin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wind that blows over the surface of the earth, wiping or paring away dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Some usage applies the word to a constantly blowing wind, while another allows it to mean simply a wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The craft or occupation of building and navigating ships or boats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term covers both ship construction and ship navigation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The constellation Argo, one of the southern constellations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical astronomical usage distinct from the ordinary meaning “ship.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: An oblong book or commonplace book.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage is reported as apparently post-classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A builder of ships or boats; a navigator or master of a ship or boat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can refer to the shipbuilder, navigator, or person in command.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular vein on the inner side of the spine, running lengthwise and connected with the heart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term; it is distinguished in the source from the similarly named saphenous vein.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bird reported in Egypt that strips a tree of its leaves.
By metaphor, any easy-riding vehicle or mount likened to a ship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of the ship meaning, distinct from the Quranic watercraft usage.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers paring or abrading a surface and the associated verbal noun.
Intensive or smoothing use of the same paring action.
Wind removes or pulverizes dust from a surface.
Wind blows over the earth’s surface in the same lexical branch.
Rough skin or other abrasive and related smoothing implements.
Wind that wipes or pares the earth’s surface.
Shipbuilding and navigation as an occupation.
Ship or boat and the astronomical constellation named for it.

cautions: The supplied Quranic evidence contains only the noun سَفِينَةٌ meaning ship or boat; the other derivatives and extensions listed here are broader Classical Arabic evidence, not additional Quranic forms.
